A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TASTE-Rob and the same three-stage pose-refinement pipeline. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original dataset analyses, video-generation comparisons, pose-refinement ablations, and simulated robot-manipulation success rates.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds grasp-type classification and hand-movement direction measurements.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the same DynamiCrafter coarse generator, image-conditioned motion diffusion refinement, and pose-conditioned regeneration. Model components, training objectives, and inference procedures are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same TASTE-Rob dataset, Ego4D training comparison, TASTE-Rob-Test evaluation, MuJoCo manipulation tasks, and qualitative examples from wild environments. The added pose metrics do not introduce new task or dataset coverage.

E2.justification: Table 3 retains consistI2V, DynamiCrafter, Open-Sora Plan, and CogVideoX. Ego4D-Gen and Coarse-TASTE-Rob also remain in their corresponding ablations; swapping table numbers does not change comparator membership.

E3.justification: Section 5.2 and Appendix 10 add GTCE and HMDA evaluation protocols. GTCE compares grasp classes using eight manipulation frames, while HMDA measures movement-direction differences against ground truth. Existing splits, training settings, and the 50 simulated manipulation tasks remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The coarse-versus-refined ablation gains checks of grasp-type correctness and movement-direction alignment, supplementing GPV's temporal-consistency assessment. Dataset comparisons and denoising-step sensitivity analyses are retained, including Table 6 after its move to the appendix.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the model comparisons. The added metrics use point estimates; GPV measures pose variation rather than uncertainty in experimental estimates.

E6.justification: v2 Table 5 adds coarse/refined GTCE results of 67.8%/9.7% and HMDA results of 26.4°/11.3°. Previously reported generation scores, GPV values, and robot success rates of 84%/96% are retained. These are additional measurements, not demonstrated performance improvements between versions.

T1.justification: Appendix 10 adds metric definitions, particularly HMDA as the mean angular discrepancy between generated and reference hand-motion vectors, alongside GTCE's grasp-class error definition. Existing diffusion equations, GPV mathematics, and pose-distribution calculations are unchanged; no proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: the 100,856-video dataset, three-stage pose refinement, and improved video generation supporting generalizable robot manipulation. The additional measurements support these existing claims.

C2.justification: Section 5.4 newly explains why pose-refinement ablations are restricted to TASTE-Rob: outputs from models fine-tuned on datasets such as Ego4D are considered too poor for reliable pose extraction. The existing limitation concerning substantial object transformations remains.

D1.justification: Appendix 10 documents the new metrics' use of HaMeR, MediaPipe, eight-frame sampling, and 17 grasp classes. The abstract expands the planned public release from the dataset to dataset plus source code through the project website; actual release is not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 adds Feix et al.'s grasp-taxonomy reference for GTCE and replaces the EPIC-KITCHENS dataset reference with the EPIC-KITCHENS-100 paper. Most other reference changes update publication metadata, while the broader research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized wording edits, integrates comparison prose into Section 5.3, expands the supplementary metric section, and adds acknowledgments. The main narrative and section sequence remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: Existing comparison figures are regrouped on page 8, supplementary figures are reordered and relocated, and Table 6 moves from the main text to the appendix. The pose-ablation table gains two metric rows. Figure content and the overall visual format are largely retained.

improvement.justification: v2 supplements GPV with ground-truth-based grasp-type and movement-direction checks in Table 5 and Appendix 10, strengthening the evidence for pose refinement. It also explains the restricted scope of that ablation. These are useful, targeted gains, although the GTCE classifier remains underspecified and the existing 100K-versus-500K MDM training-step discrepancy remains unresolved.
